Definition: Tirshatha, the title of a Persian deputy or governor
BiblicalUsage: Tirshatha is a title, not a name: the Persian governor's office. The Tirshatha tells the returned exiles they shall not eat of the most holy things until a priest stands up with Urim and Thummim, and the same ruling is repeated in Nehemiah's list.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the title shows how carefully the return was ordered: even the governor would not decide who might eat the holy things, but waited for the priest and the lots.
